item.title: Israeli opposition leader Eisenkot says Netanyahu 'failed' to discredit election results
item.description:
Israeli opposition leader Eisenkot says Netanyahu 'failed' to discredit election results

Israel’s Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot said that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his party "failed" to discredit Israeli election results. 

"The vile and malicious attempt to deny the election results, to undermine the will of the public, to smear an entire public, and to drag Israel into additional elections has failed," he said in a post on X.

"Only someone who understands that they have lost would embark on such a brazen campaign of delegitimisation - even at the cost of further eroding public trust in the state's institutions."

He described the recent election results "clear and unequivocal", and urged Israeli citizens to "ignore the background noise".

"The people are sovereign, and they have spoken: the government of failure has no majority and it has lost," he added, referring to Netanyahu's government.

Israel intentionally released footage of Mossad operatives in Iran to provoke mass arrests, ex-chief says
item.description:
Israel intentionally released footage of Mossad operatives in Iran to provoke mass arrests, ex-chief says

Former Mossad chief David Barnea has said Israel intentionally released images of their covert operation in Iran during the June 2025 conflict to provoke mass arrests and make it harder for Iranian forces to find real Israeli agents.

“One of the reasons we immediately released an official video on the morning of Operation Rising Lion, with the Mossad logo, was to protect the agents who were there,” Barnea said, according to comments The Jerusalem Post reported on 25 October.

Barnea said the leak of the footage of Israeli operations in Iran was not just an attempt to showcase the Mossad’s reach but also a strategy to overwhelm Iranian counterintelligence, causing them to make mass arrests, making it more difficult to distinguish operatives from ordinary citizens.

“We wanted to make sure they arrested so many people in Iran that they wouldn’t be able to distinguish the wheat from the chaff and would eventually release everyone,” he said.

Barnea said Iranian authorities arrested 21,000 people during the operation.

Read more: Israel intentionally released footage of Mossad operatives in Iran to provoke mass arrests, ex-chief says

item.title: UKMTO says vessel hit by two projectiles near Saudi Arabia
item.description:
UKMTO says vessel hit by two projectiles near Saudi Arabia

A tanker travelling south east through the Gulf was struck by two unidentified projectiles on its port side, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) agency said.

The incident occurred 72 nautical miles east of Saudi Arabia's Ras al-Khafji. UKMTO added that All crew members were accounted for and no environmental impact had been reported.

item.title: Qatar condemns attack on LNG tanker in Gulf, warns of threat to global energy supplies
item.description: Qatar on Sunday strongly condemned an attack on the liquefied natural gas (LNG) tanker Al Mayeda while it was sailing in the Gulf, warning that the incident threatened maritime navigation and global energy supplies, Anadolu reports. In a statement, the Foreign Ministry said the vessel belonged to Qatar Gas Transport Company, known as Nakilat. The ministry described the attack as “a dangerous act that threatens the safety of maritime navigation and the security of global energy supplies.” Qatar “reserves the right to take all necessary measures under international law and the UN Charter to protect its property, safeguard its interests and ensure the safety of its vessels and crews,” it said. item.title: At least 8 Palestinians killed in new Israeli violations of Gaza ceasefire
item.description: Eight Palestinians, including a child, were killed and others wounded in Israeli attacks across the Gaza Strip on Sunday amid Israel’s daily violations of last year’s ceasefire, a medical source said, Anadolu reports. The source at Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis, southern Gaza, told Anadolu that five Palestinians were killed in an airstrike in al-Mawasi, west of the city. Local sources said that the strike hit near schools for children, causing panic among them. In a separate attack, a medical source at al-Shifa Hospital in Gaza City said three Palestinians, including a child, were killed in an Israeli airstrike on al-Thawra Street. item.title: Muhammad Hazem Salah Abou Ismail, Lawyer, Scholar and 2012 Egyptian Presidential Candidate, Faces Imminent Threat to Life in Egypt’s Badr Prison
item.description: Press Release Muhammad Hazem Salah Abou Ismail was born on 16 June 1961 and has been registered with the Egyptian Bar Association under registration number 54053 since 1990. He is a practising human rights lawyer known for representing individuals and groups subjected to repression and persecution, including opposition figures and activists. He has pursued public interest cases and engaged in legal action against alleged human rights violations. He also stood as an independent presidential candidate in the 2012 presidential elections held in Egypt. Mr. Abou Ismail was arrested on 5 July 2013, two days after the military coup of 3 July 2013. item.title: Israeli army builds new roads linking military posts in southern Lebanon
item.description: The Israeli army is building new roads through mountains and valleys in southern Lebanon to connect its military positions, Lebanon’s National News Agency (NNA) reported Saturday, Anadolu reports. The work spans the western and central sectors of southern Lebanon, where Israeli forces have established military posts on occupied Lebanese territory, according to the agency. NNA said the construction was taking place alongside Israeli demolition operations in the area. The central sector includes the towns of Aita al-Shaab, Maroun al-Ras, Bint Jbeil and Aitaroun. Maroun al-Ras overlooks the Israeli settlement of Avivim across the border.
